source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 3.2 gives bivariate identification from one perfect intervention per node under the continuous-witness condition (3.2); Theorem 3.4 uses paired interventions per node in arbitrary dimension; Section 7 conjectures the one-per-node extension for n greater than 2.
CauCA's principal component-recovery result uses a supplied graph and intervention-target information; one perfect intervention per node yields elementwise recovery in that known-structure class.
Theorem 3.4 identifies a maximal measurement model under a complete intervention family and a no-imaginary-subset condition, up to isolated latent edges.

Theorem 1 identifies the model up to permutation and scaling from unknown-target perfect single-node interventions under nonlinear mixing, while the latent model is Gaussian and hence linear SEM-based.

The article develops MMD two-sample testing and concentration for observed samples, not fitted likelihood-ratio values reused across graph edges.
The paper supplies uniform local-linear conditional-distribution bias, rate, and asymptotic-expansion results with observed response and covariate arguments.

The paper studies nonparametric regression with nonparametrically generated covariates and derives stochastic expansions, but does not address generated indicator thresholds in conditional-CDF estimation.

The paper obtains representation-identification results from perfect do interventions through support geometry, with polynomial-mixing and related support restrictions; it is not the proposed unknown-target arbitrary-diffeomorphic ratio-order regime.
